Name of the Surah

• It is called Al-Insan (Man), because it opens with mention of man and his creation from nothing, and the creation of the goods of the earth that he needs.

Some of the Surah's Aims

• Demonstrating God's power in creating man and preparing him to carry out the worship he was charged with: God gave him hearing, sight and the senses. It also states that he is commanded to single out God for worship, in gratitude to his Creator, and warns against associating partners with God, and affirms recompense in both cases.

• Mention of the bliss that God has prepared in the Hereafter for the people of happiness, and mention of some of their attributes: such as fulfilling vows, feeding the poor seeking the pleasure of God, and fearing the punishment of God.

• Strengthening the Prophet (ﷺ) to bear the burdens of the message, commanding him to be patient with what befalls him in that cause, and warning him not to be soft toward the disbelievers; and that his being chosen for the message is a great blessing, to be thanked by turning to the worship of God by night and day.

[Tafsir]

A long span of time passed over man before the soul was breathed into him, during which he was not anything worth mentioning, and no trace of him was known.

This passage is from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, the commentary produced by the King Fahd Complex. Here is the translation of its explanation of verses 2–3 of Surah al-Insan (76):

We created man from a mixed drop of the man's fluid and the woman's fluid, testing him with the legal obligations afterwards. For this purpose We made him one who hears and one who sees, so that he would hear the signs and see the proofs. We have made clear to him and made him know the path of guidance and misguidance, and of good and evil, so that he would be either a believer who is grateful, or one who is ungrateful and denies.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 76, verse 4:

Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains of iron with which their feet are bound, and shackles with which their hands are fettered to their necks, and a Fire in which they will be burned.

Indeed, the people of obedience and sincerity, who fulfil God's right, will drink on the Day of Resurrection from a cup containing wine mixed with the finest kinds of perfume, which is the water of kafur (camphor).

This cup mixed with camphor is a spring from which the servants of God drink; they make it flow wherever they wish, flowing easily.

These were the ones who, in the world, fulfilled what they had made obligatory upon themselves of obedience to God, and feared the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, whose harm is grave and whose evil is widespread and spreading among people, except for those whom God has mercy upon. And they feed the food despite their love for it and their need for it: the poor person who is unable to earn and has nothing sufficient to meet his needs, the orphan whose father has died while he is below the age of puberty and has no wealth, and the prisoner taken captive in war from the polytheists and others. And they say to themselves: "We only feed you seeking the pleasure of God and desiring His reward; we do not want any compensation from you, nor do we intend praise or thanks from you. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is severely distressing, on which faces will frown and foreheads will be furrowed from the awfulness of its matter and the severity of its terror."

Then Allah protected them from the hardships of that Day, gave them radiance and brightness in their faces, and joy and happiness in their hearts. And in recompense for their patience in worship during the world, He gave them a great Garden, where they eat whatever they wish, and wear fine silk garments, reclining therein upon couches adorned with splendid clothing and curtains. Round about these righteous ones, to serve them, will go boys who remain ever in their youthful state. When you see them, you would think them—because of their beauty, the clearness of their complexions and the brightness of their faces—scattered pearls, shining.
And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great kingdom, vast and without limit.

Above them will be garments covering them and adorning their bodies, their linings of fine green silk and their outer layers of thick silk. They will be adorned with bracelets of silver. Their Lord will give them to drink, beyond that bliss, a drink free of any impurity or defilement.
It will be said to them: "This has been prepared for you in return for your righteous deeds, and your deeds in the world were pleasing and accepted in the sight of Allah."
Indeed, We have sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur'an as a sending down from Us, so that you may remind the people with what it contains of promise and threat, and of reward and punishment.

So be patient with the decree of your Lord, the qadari decree (the decree of predestination), and accept it. For His religious command, the dini command (the legislated law), persevere in following it. Do not obey any of the disbelievers who is immersed in desires or extreme in disbelief and misguidance. Persist in remembering the name of your Lord and in calling upon Him at the beginning and the end of the day.

So be patient with the decree of your Lord, the qadari decree (the decree of predestination), and accept it. For His religious command, the dini command (the legislated law), persevere in following it. Do not obey any of the disbelievers who is immersed in desires or extreme in disbelief and misguidance. Persist in remembering the name of your Lord and in calling upon Him at the beginning and the end of the day.
And during the night, submit humbly to your Lord, pray to Him, and perform the night prayer (tahajjud) to Him for a long portion of it.

Indeed, these polytheists love this worldly life and are occupied with it, and they leave behind them the work for the Hereafter, and what would bring them salvation on a great Day of severe hardships.
We created them and strengthened their creation. If We wish, We can destroy them and bring in a people who are obedient and who comply with the commands of Allah.

This surah, with its encouragement and warning, its promise and threat, is an admonition to all the worlds. Whoever wants good for himself in this world and the Hereafter should take, through faith and God-consciousness (taqwa), a path that leads him to the forgiveness of Allah and His pleasure. You do not will anything except by the decree (taqdir) and will of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of the conditions of His creation, All-Wise in His management and His making. He admits whomever He wills of His servants into His mercy and pleasure, and they are the believers. And He has prepared for the wrongdoers, who transgress the limits of Allah, a painful punishment.
